lessons.title: Aşama 1 · Simple Present ve have/has
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda alışkanlıkların, genel doğrular ve sahip olduğun şeyler (ağrılar dahil) hakkında olumlu, olumsuz ve soru cümleleri kurabileceksin.

grammar.title: Simple Present: olumlu cümle
grammar.summary: Rutinler, alışkanlıklar, genel doğrular ve sevdiğimiz şeyler için kullanılır. I/You/We/They + V1 → I work. He/She/It + V1-s → She works. Yazım: go → goes, watch → watches, do → does, study → studies; ama play → plays. people çoğuldur → People are / People work.
examples: I work from home.
She works from home.
Water boils at 100 degrees.

grammar.title: Olumsuz ve soru: do / does
grammar.summary: Olumsuz → Özne + don't/doesn't + V1. Soru → Do/Does + özne + V1? does veya doesn't gelince fiildeki -s gider: She works → She doesn't work → Does she work? Kısa cevap: Yes, I do. / No, she doesn't. 'Katılıyorum' gibi fiillerde am/is/are kullanılmaz: I agree.
examples: I don't drink coffee.
Does she work on Sundays?
Do you draw? - Yes, I do.

grammar.title: have / has (sahiplik ve ağrılar)
grammar.summary: I/You/We/They → have / don't have. He/She/It → has / doesn't have (doesn't has değil!). Türkçede 'başım ağrıyor' deriz ama İngilizcede ağrı ve belirtiler için have kullanılır: I have a headache. Dış görünüşte de: She has long hair.
examples: He has a good house.
She doesn't have much free time.
I have a sore throat.

lessons.title: Aşama 2 · Günlük rutin ve sıklık zarfları
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda günlük rutinini ve bir şeyi ne sıklıkla yaptığını doğru kelime sırasıyla anlatabileceksin.

grammar.title: Sıklık zarfları ve yerleri
grammar.summary: always (%100) → usually → normally/often → sometimes → occasionally → rarely/seldom → hardly ever → never (%0). Normal fiil: Özne + zarf + fiil → I usually drink coffee. To be: Özne + am/is/are + zarf → I am usually tired. never zaten olumsuzdur; yanına don't gelmez.
examples: I always eat breakfast.
I sometimes draw at night.
She is always hungry.

grammar.title: How often? ve zaman ifadeleri
grammar.summary: How often do you + V1? → Ne sıklıkla...? Cevaplar: every day, once a week, twice a week, three times a week, on weekends. Dikkat: I don't always play (her zaman oynamam) ≠ I never play (hiç oynamam).
examples: How often do you exercise?
I work out three times a week.
What do you usually do in the morning?

lessons.title: Aşama 3 · Present Continuous (şu an olanlar)
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda şu anda olan şeyleri anlatabilecek ve Simple Present ile Present Continuous arasında doğru seçim yapabileceksin.

grammar.title: am / is / are + V-ing
grammar.summary: Konuşma anında olan şeyler. I am + V-ing; He/She/It is + V-ing; You/We/They are + V-ing. Olumsuz: am not / isn't / aren't + V-ing. Soru: Am/Is/Are + özne + V-ing? be atlanmaz (I cooking ❌). Yazım: make → making, sit → sitting, lie → lying. İpucu kelimeler: now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!
examples: I'm cooking dinner right now.
Look! The children are playing in the garden.
They aren't playing football at the moment.

grammar.title: Simple Present mı, Present Continuous mu?
grammar.summary: Rutin, alışkanlık ve genel gerçek → Simple Present: I work from home. Water boils at 100°C. Şu an veya bu aralar → Present Continuous: I'm working on a new project these days. Soru farkı: What do you do? = Ne iş yapıyorsun? / What are you doing? = Şu an ne yapıyorsun? Durum fiilleri (like, love, want, know, need, understand) genelde -ing almaz: I want a coffee ✅, I am wanting ❌.
examples: I usually work from home, but today I'm working in a café.
What do you do? – I'm a designer.
What are you doing? – I'm watching a video.

grammar.title: Planlanmış yakın gelecek
grammar.summary: Takvimde belli olan, ayarlanmış planlar için de Present Continuous kullanılır: I'm meeting my friends tonight. We're flying to London next month. Bu kullanımda zaman ifadesi (tonight, tomorrow, next week) mutlaka olur.
examples: I'm meeting my friends tonight.
We're travelling to London next month.

lessons.title: Aşama 4 · In / On / At (zaman ve yer)
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda saat, gün, ay, yıl ve yer bildirirken in, on ve at'i doğru seçebileceksin.

grammar.title: Zaman: at / on / in
grammar.summary: AT → saat ve nokta zamanlar: at 8, at noon, at midnight, at night. ON → günler ve tarihler: on Monday, on weekends, on May 5th, on my birthday. IN → ay, yıl, mevsim, gün bölümleri: in September, in 2026, in summer, in the morning. İstisna: in the morning / in the evening ama at night. Ezber: at 9 → on Monday → in September.
examples: I wake up at 8.
I usually relax on weekends.
I started learning English in 2026.

grammar.title: Yer ve ulaşım
grammar.summary: AT → belirli nokta/konum: at home, at work, at the gym, at the airport. IN → bir alanın içi: in the room, in the car, in Istanbul, in Turkey. ON → yüzey: on the table, on the wall, on the floor. Ulaşım: küçük/özel araç → in the car, in a taxi; toplu taşıma → on the bus, on the train, on the plane.
examples: I am at home.
My phone is on the table.
I'm on the bus.

grammar.title: at the beginning of / at the end of
grammar.summary: Bir şeyin başı ve sonu: the + beginning / end + of + the + isim. the başta da sonda da gerekir (beginning of month ❌ → the beginning of the month). Zaman olarak genelde at ile kullanılır: at the beginning of the class, at the end of the month. in the end (of olmadan) = sonunda, en sonunda: In the end, we stayed home. start de olur: the start of the movie.
examples: I missed the beginning of the movie.
We have a short test at the end of the class.
I pay my bills at the beginning of the month.

lessons.title: Aşama 5 · Zamirler ve sahiplik (he / him / his)
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda bir kişiyi cümledeki görevine göre doğru kelimeyle (he / him / his / his) gösterebileceksin.

grammar.title: Özne ve nesne: he – him
grammar.summary: İşi yapan kişi → özne: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. İş o kişiye yapılıyorsa (fiilden veya with/to/for gibi edattan sonra) → nesne: me, you, him, her, it, us, them. He called me. → I called him. Hafıza: He → Him → His = O → Onu/Ona → Onun.
examples: He invited me.
I called him.
I went with him.

grammar.title: Sahiplik: his car / this car is his
grammar.summary: my / your / his / her / its / our / their + İSİM → my car. mine / yours / his / hers / ours / theirs → isim YOK → The car is mine. her iki görevlidir: I called her (nesne) / her car (sahiplik). its = onun (nesne/hayvan), it's = it is / it has; sahiplikte kesme işareti yoktur.
examples: This is my car. / This car is mine.
Their office is large. / This office is theirs.
The dog is eating its food.

lessons.title: Aşama 6 · Simple Past ve was/were
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda dün ve geçmişte olanları olumlu, olumsuz ve soru cümleleriyle anlatabilecek, did ile was/were'i ayırt edebileceksin.

grammar.title: V1 – V2 – V3
grammar.summary: V1 = yalın hal (Simple Present, can/did/will sonrası). V2 = Simple Past olumlu cümle. V3 = have/has + V3 (Present Perfect). Düzenli fiiller -ed alır: work – worked – worked. Düzensizler ezberlenir: go – went – gone, see – saw – seen, eat – ate – eaten, make – made – made, dye – dyed – dyed.
examples: I work every day. (V1)
I worked yesterday. (V2)
I have worked here before. (V3)

grammar.title: Simple Past: V2 ve did
grammar.summary: Olumlu → Özne + V2: I went home. Olumsuz → Özne + didn't + V1. Soru → Did + özne + V1? did/didn't geçmişi zaten gösterir, fiil V1 kalır: I didn't went ❌ → I didn't go ✅. Zaman ifadeleri: yesterday, last night, last week, two days ago, in 2025.
examples: I went to the gym yesterday.

lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda planlarını, anlık kararlarını, tahminlerini ve 'eğer ... olursa' cümlelerini kurabileceksin.

grammar.title: will / be going to
grammar.summary: will + V1 → o anda verilen karar, tahmin, söz/teklif: I'm tired. I will go home. Olumsuz: won't (will not). am/is/are + going to + V1 → önceden plan/niyet: I'm going to study tonight. Soru: Will you ...? / Are you going to ...? will'den sonra can gelmez → will be able to.
examples: I will help you.
I think it will rain tomorrow.
I am going to study English tonight.

grammar.title: Tahmin kalıpları
grammar.summary: There's a good chance that + özne + will + V1 → büyük ihtimalle (güçlü ihtimal). It's possible that ... → olabilir (sadece mümkün). It's possible that she's busy right now. Geçmiş için: It's possible that he forgot.
examples: There's a good chance that the exam will be hard.

It's possible that he forgot about the meeting.

grammar.title: First Conditional: If + present, will + V1
grammar.summary: Gerçekleşmesi mümkün gelecek durumlar: If + Simple Present, will + V1. If tarafında will kullanılmaz: If it will rain ❌ → If it rains ✅. Sıra değişebilir: I will stay home if it rains. (If başta ise virgül konur.) Gerçekçi olmayan hayaller (1 milyon dolarım olsa) için başka yapı kullanılır: If I had..., I would... (ileride).
examples: If it rains, I will stay home.

What will you do if you can't sleep tonight?

I want to go. (gitmek istiyorum) / I won't go. (gitmeyeceğim). want'tan sonra to gelir, won't'tan sonra direkt V1. Gelecekte yapabilmek: will be able to (will can ❌): I'll be able to... / I won't be able to... make it = (bir yere / bir şeye) yetişmek, gidebilmek. by + zaman = en geç o saatte: by 8 = en geç 8'de. until = o zamana kadar devam eden bir durum için: I'll wait until 8.

grammar.title: can / can't / be able to

grammar.title: good at / talent for / also

I can draw (çizebilirim) / I am good at drawing (çizimde iyiyim) / I have a talent for drawing (yeteneğim var). also: normal fiilden önce (I also draw), can ve am/is/are'den sonra (I can also paint / I am also interested).

lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda duygularını ve korkularını doğru sıfat ve edatlarla anlatabileceksin.

grammar.title: -ed / -ing sıfatlar
grammar.summary: -ed → duyguyu hisseden kişi: I am bored. -ing → o duyguyu yaratan şey: The lesson is boring. Çiftler: interested/interesting, excited/exciting, tired/tiring, confused/confusing, embarrassed/embarrassing, frustrated/frustrating. Her -ing şimdiki zaman değildir; cümlenin tamamına bak.

lessons.title: Aşama 12 · Present Perfect
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda hayat tecrübelerini anlatabilecek ve Simple Past ile Present Perfect arasında doğru seçim yapabileceksin.

grammar.title: have / has + V3
grammar.summary: I/You/We/They + have + V3; He/She/It + has + V3. Olumsuz: haven't/hasn't + V3. Soru: Have/Has + özne + V3? Kullanım: 1) hayat tecrübesi (Have you ever been to Japan?), 2) zamanı belirsiz geçmiş (I have finished my work.), 3) etkisi şimdi süren olay (I have lost my keys.).

grammar.title: ever / never / just / already / yet / before
grammar.summary: ever = hiç (soruda), never = hiç/asla (olumlu fiille), just = az önce, already = çoktan/zaten, yet = henüz (olumsuz ve soruda, cümle sonunda), before = daha önce. been to = gidip gelmiş; gone to = gitmiş, hâlâ orada.
examples: I have never tried sushi.

grammar.title: Simple Past mı, Present Perfect mi?
grammar.summary: Zaman belli (yesterday, last week, two days ago, in 2025) → Simple Past: I saw it yesterday. Zaman önemsiz veya şimdiyle bağlantılı → Present Perfect: I have seen it before. Belli zaman ifadesiyle Present Perfect kullanılmaz: I have seen him yesterday ❌.
examples: I went to Italy in 2025.
I have been to Italy.
I have been to the gym three times this week.

grammar.title: for / since ve already, yet, ever nerede durur?
grammar.summary: Türkçedeki '...dır / ...den beri' → Present Perfect: I have lived here for five years (5 yıldır burada yaşıyorum; I live here for five years ❌). for + süre (for three years, for a long time). since + başlangıç noktası (since 2020, since Monday, since I was a child). Kelime sırası: already, ever, never, just → have ile V3 arasına: I have already eaten. Have you ever tried it? yet → cümle sonuna, olumsuz ve soruda: I haven't finished yet. Have you finished yet? Belli zaman + 'henüz' birlikte: I cleaned my room yesterday, but I haven't cleaned the kitchen yet.

lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda insanları ve şeyleri tanımlayıp karşılaştırabilecek, 'en ...' cümleleri kurabileceksin.

grammar.title: Comparative: -er / more ... than
grammar.summary: İki şey karşılaştırılır. Kısa sıfat + -er + than: taller than. Uzun sıfat → more + sıfat + than: more expensive than. Yazım: big → bigger, happy → happier, nice → nicer, scary → scarier. Düzensiz: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further. -er ile more birlikte kullanılmaz (more taller ❌). much / a lot / a bit + comparative.
examples: A plane is faster than a car.

grammar.title: Superlative ve as ... as
grammar.summary: Grup içinde 'en': the + sıfat-est (the tallest), the most + uzun sıfat (the most important). good → the best, bad → the worst. the'yi unutma. Kalıp: the ...-est ... I have ever seen. Eşitlik: as + sıfat + as; eşit değil: not as + sıfat + as.

grammar.title: Görünüş ve kişilik
grammar.summary: Görünüş: be + sıfat (He is tall. She is slim.) veya have/has + isim (She has long hair. He has dark hair.). Kişilik: She is talkative / reliable / patient. Kalıplar: A good teacher should be ... / For me, a good teacher is someone who ...

lessons.title: Aşama 15 · Prefer, would prefer ve would rather (tercihler)
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda genel tercihlerini (prefer), kibar ve o ana özel tercihlerini (would prefer) ve güçlü kişisel seçimlerini (would rather) doğru kalıplarla söyleyebileceksin.

grammar.title: prefer: genel tercih (her zaman, genelde)
grammar.summary: prefer = bir şeyi diğerine genel olarak tercih etmek. Üç kalıp var: (1) prefer + isim + to + isim: I prefer coffee to tea. (2) prefer + V-ing + to + V-ing: I prefer reading to watching TV. (3) prefer + to V1 + rather than + V1: I prefer to stay home rather than go out. Türkçedeki 'çaya' (-e hali) İngilizcede to olur; than değil (prefer coffee than tea ❌). to V1 kullanırsan ikinci kısım rather than + V1 olur (prefer to watch than read ❌). Genel tercih = Simple Present: she prefers (-s!).
examples: I prefer coffee to tea.
She prefers reading to watching TV.
I prefer to stay home rather than go out.
I prefer playing games to listening to music.

grammar.title: would prefer ('d prefer): kibar, bu seferlik tercih
grammar.summary: would prefer genel bir alışkanlık değil, belirli bir durumdaki seçimdir: bu akşam, yarın, şu an, bir teklif karşısında. Daha kibar ve resmîdir. Kalıplar: would prefer + to V1 (en yaygın): I'd prefer to meet tomorrow. would prefer + isim: We'd prefer a window seat. (would prefer + V-ing de olur ama daha az yaygın.) Soru: Would you prefer tea or coffee? Kural: 'genelde' diyorsan prefer, 'bu sefer / şimdi' diyorsan would prefer. I would prefer riding motorcycles (bağlam yok) → genel tercihse I prefer riding motorcycles.
examples: I'd prefer to meet tomorrow.
We'd prefer a window seat.
Would you like coffee? – I'd prefer orange juice, please.
I'd prefer to go out this weekend.

grammar.title: would rather ('d rather) + V1 (than + V1)
grammar.summary: would rather = belirli bir durumda bir seçeneği diğerine tercih etmek; would prefer'dan daha kişisel ve güçlü. Arkasından yalın fiil (V1) gelir: to yok, -ing yok (would rather to go ❌, would rather going ❌). Karşılaştırma için than + V1: I'd rather stay home than go out tonight. Olumsuzu: would rather not + V1 (would rather not to ❌, wouldn't rather ❌). Soru: Would you rather ... or ...? Kısa cevap: I'd rather not. ('d burada would demek.)
examples: I'd rather stay home than go out tonight.
They would rather not talk about it now.
Would you rather ride a motorcycle or drive a car?
Do you want to come? – I'd rather not.

grammar.title: would rather + özne + V2 (başkasının ne yapmasını istediğin)
grammar.summary: Kendi tercihini söylerken V1: I'd rather go. Başka birinin bir şey yapmasını tercih ediyorsan: would rather + (that) + özne + V2. Fiil geçmiş görünür ama anlam şimdi / gelecektir: She'd rather you called her later (Daha sonra aramanı tercih eder). Olumsuzu didn't + V1: I'd rather you didn't tell anyone (Kimseye söylemesen iyi olur). Kibarca 'yapma' demenin yoludur.
examples: She'd rather you called her later.
I'd rather you didn't tell anyone about this.
I'd rather go now. / I'd rather you went now.

grammar.title: Hızlı karşılaştırma ve tipik hatalar
grammar.summary: prefer: genel tercih, nötr (I prefer art to geography). would prefer: kibar / belirli durum, isteklerde ve planlarda (I'd prefer to leave earlier tomorrow). would rather: belirli bir durumda güçlü kişisel seçim (I'd rather not go out tonight). Kalıp özeti: prefer A to B · prefer to V1 rather than V1 · would prefer to V1 · would rather V1 (than V1). Tipik hatalar: I prefer coffee than tea ❌ → to tea. I prefer to watch than read ❌ → rather than read. I would rather to go ❌ → would rather go. I'd rather going ❌ → I'd rather go. Cevap verirken: I don't mind / Either is fine (fark etmez), It's up to you (sana kalmış).

We'd prefer to leave earlier tomorrow.
I'd rather not go out tonight.
Tea or coffee? – I don't mind. Either is fine.

grammar.title: Fikrini söylemek (6 kalıp)
grammar.summary: 1) I think (that) ... = Bence / Sanırım 2) In my opinion, ... = Bence (biraz daha resmi) 3) I feel like ... = Bana öyle geliyor ki (konuşma dili) 4) If you ask me, ... = Bana sorarsan (ask to me ❌) 5) As far as I'm concerned, ... = Bana kalırsa (kesin fikir) 6) Personally, ... = Şahsen. Kural: fikir için I think, I'm thinking ❌ (I'm thinking = şu an kafamda düşünüyorum: I'm thinking about my weekend.) Olumsuz fikirde olumsuzluk think'e gelir: I don't think it's a good idea. Kısa cevap: I don't think so. Kural: agree bir FİİLDİR: I agree / I don't agree / Do you agree? (I am agree ❌, Are you agree ❌). agree with + kişi/fikir. Zıttı: disagree.

lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda make a decision, find out, give up, deal with gibi 20 sık kalıbı doğru fiil, doğru edat ve doğru fiil biçimiyle (V-ing) kullanabileceksin.

grammar.title: make / take / keep / be: kalıbı bütün olarak ezberle
grammar.summary: make a decision (karar vermek; do a decision ❌; make a decision to + V1: She made a decision to learn English). make progress (ilerleme kaydetmek): progress sayılamaz, a progress ❌, progresses ❌; make progress in English. take a look at (bir göz atmak; look at ile aynı edat: at). keep in mind (aklında tutmak): Keep in mind that... / Keep my advice in mind. be careful with (... -e dikkat et, özenli ol): Be careful with that glass / with your money. Önceden gördüklerin: take part in (katılmak; take part to ❌, 14. aşama), take advantage of (yararlanmak; ama insan için 'suistimal etmek': Don't take advantage of people's kindness, 14. aşama).
examples: I need to make a decision about my future.

You can make progress if you practice every day.
Be careful with that glass. It's very expensive.

grammar.title: Ayrılabilen phrasal verb'ler: put it on (put on it ❌)
grammar.summary: put on, find out, figure out, bring up, give up ayrılabilir: nesne isimse iki yere de girer (Put on your jacket / Put your jacket on). Nesne zamirse (it, them, him) mutlaka araya girer: Put it on ✅, Put on it ❌; I can't figure it out ✅. Ayrılmayanlar: look after (I look after her; look her after ❌), come across (rastlamak), deal with, carry on. find ≠ find out: find = kaybolan bir şeyi bulmak (I found my keys); find out = bir bilgiyi öğrenmek, ortaya çıkarmak (We found out the truth). learn = ders / beceri öğrenmek (learn English). find out + soru kelimesi: dolaylı soruda düz sıra: find out why she is sad (why is she ❌). come across insan için de olur ama 'eski bir arkadaşa rastladım' için en doğalı run into / bump into.
examples: Put on your jacket. It's cold outside.
Where's my jacket? I want to put it on.
I want to find out why she is sad.
I came across an old photo in a box.

grammar.title: give up smoking, carry on studying, get used to waking up
grammar.summary: Bu kalıplardan sonra fiil gelirse V-ing olur: give up + V-ing (bırakmak: gave up smoking; give up to smoke ❌). carry on + V-ing (devam etmek: carried on studying) ya da carry on with + isim (carry on with your homework). get used to + isim / V-ing (alışmak: getting used to waking up; get used to wake up ❌). Burada to bir edat, look forward to ve be used to (8. aşama) ile aynı aile. Karıştırma: I used to wake up early = Eskiden erken kalkardım (+ V1). be proud of + V-ing: I'm proud of passing the exam. give up on = birinden / bir hayalden vazgeçmek, umudu kesmek: Don't give up on your dreams (give up from ❌).
examples: My father gave up smoking last year.
She was tired, but she carried on studying.
I'm getting used to waking up early.
Don't give up on your dreams.

grammar.title: Sabit edatlar: deal with, depend on, be proud of
grammar.summary: Türkçedeki hâl ekine bakıp edat seçme, kalıbı ezberle. deal with (başa çıkmak, uğraşmak; deal stress ❌): I don't know how to deal with stress. depend on (... -e bağlı olmak / güvenmek; depend of ❌, depend from ❌): Our plans depend on the weather. Kısaca: It depends. = Duruma göre. be proud of (... ile gurur duymak; proud with ❌, proud on ❌): My parents are proud of me. look after (bakmak, = take care of): Can you look after my cat? settle down (sakinleşmek: Please settle down; ya da yerleşip düzen kurmak: settle down in a small town).

grammar.title: Teklif ve fikirlere tepki: varım, yokum, kararsızım
grammar.summary: Kabul: I'm in! / I'm down! (gündelik, = I'm in) / Sounds good (Sounds well ❌). Ret: Count me out (Beni saymayın, ben yokum). Kararsızlık: I'm torn (between A and B) = iki arada kaldım; I'm on the fence = kararsızım. Tartışmada: You have a point = bunda haklısın (19. aşamadaki That's a good point gibi); Fair enough = peki, mantıklı; That's a stretch = bu biraz zorlama; I'm not buying it = yemezler, buna inanmıyorum; Don't get me wrong, ... = beni yanlış anlama (Don't understand me wrong ❌).
examples: We're going to the beach on Saturday. – I'm in!

grammar.title: Durumunu anlatmak: I'm + kelime
grammar.summary: I'm broke = beş parasızım (broken = kırık, I'm broken ❌). I'm swamped = işten başımı kaldıramıyorum. I'm running late = gecikiyorum (şu an olan iş → Present Continuous; lately = son zamanlarda, karıştırma). I'm fed up with + isim / V-ing = ... -den bıktım (fed up from ❌). I'm all ears = can kulağıyla dinliyorum. I'm over it = atlattım, geride bıraktım. I'm cooked = (argo) mahvoldum, işim bitti. Tuzak: I'm down (for it) = varım; ama I'm feeling down = moralim bozuk.

Sohbet: Keep me posted = beni haberdar et; Hit me up = bana yaz; Long story short = uzun lafın kısası; It rings a bell = kulağa tanıdık geliyor; I can't help it = elimde değil (can't help + V-ing: I can't help laughing). Bunların çoğu arkadaş dili: iş e-postasında My bad, Hit me up, I'm cooked yerine Sorry, Please contact me, I'm in trouble yaz.

lessons.title: Aşama 24 · Deyimler (idioms)
lessons.goal: Bu aşamanın sonunda a piece of cake, break the ice, under the weather gibi 17 yaygın deyimin gerçek anlamını bilip cümle içinde doğru zamanla kullanabileceksin.

grammar.title: Deyimler kelime kelime çevrilmez, kalıp sabittir
grammar.summary: Deyimin anlamı parçalardan çıkmaz ve kelimeleri değiştirilmez: a piece of cake (a cake piece ❌) = çocuk oyuncağı; cost an arm and a leg (an arm and leg ❌) = dünyanın parası tutmak; once in a blue moon = kırk yılda bir; out of the blue = birdenbire. Bazılarının Türkçede birebir karşılığı var: break the ice = buzları eritmek (break the ices ❌), spill the beans = ağzından baklayı çıkarmak, bite the bullet = dişini sıkmak, The ball is in your court = top sende (on your court ❌), miss the boat = fırsatı (treni) kaçırmak.

She spilled the beans. I'm going to hit the sack (hit – hit – hit). Let's call it a day. Sahiplik değişebilir: The ball is in my / your / their court. be on the same page: Are we on the same page? see eye to eye çoğunlukla olumsuz kullanılır: My brother and I don't see eye to eye (on politics).

lessons.title: Aşama 25 · Fiil + to + fiil (want to, decide to, manage to...)
lessons.goal: want, need, decide, try, forget, manage gibi 20 fiilden sonra to + V1 kullanmak; to'dan sonra -ing, -s veya V2 kullanmamak; help (to), would like to ve can't afford to gibi zor kalıpları doğru kurmak.

grammar.title: Kural: fiil + to + V1 (to'dan sonra fiil hep yalın)
grammar.summary: Bu fiillerden sonra ikinci fiil to + V1 olur: want to, need to, decide to, plan to, hope to, try to, learn to, forget to, remember to, promise to, agree to, refuse to, manage to, offer to, expect to, prefer to, choose to, would like to, can't afford to. Çekim ekini (-s, -ed) sadece ilk fiil alır, to'dan sonraki fiil hiç değişmez: She wants to buy ✅ (wants to buys ❌), He tried to speak ✅ (tried to spoke ❌), She learned to swim ✅ (learned to swimming ❌). to'yu da atlama: She wants buy ❌. Türkçedeki '-meyi / -mek / -meye' ekinin karşılığı çoğu zaman bu to + V1. Dikkat: can, will, must gibi modal'lardan sonra to yok (can to ❌), ama want / need / have'den sonra to var.
examples: I want to buy a new phone.
She wants to spend more time with her family.
He tries to understand my feelings.
She learned to swim last summer.

grammar.title: Anlama göre gruplar
grammar.summary: İstek ve plan: want to, would like to, need to, plan to, hope to, expect to (bir şeyin olacağını düşünmek / beklemek). Karar ve seçim: decide to, choose to, prefer to. Çaba ve sonuç: try to (-meye çalışmak), learn to (-meyi öğrenmek), manage to (zor bir şeyi başarmak; tek seferlik başarı için could yerine: I managed to catch the bus). Söz ve tepki: promise to (-eceğine söz vermek), agree to (-meyi kabul etmek), refuse to (-meyi reddetmek), offer to (-meyi teklif etmek). Hafıza: forget to, remember to. Para: can / can't afford to. İpucu: Türkçede 'söz verdi, kabul etti, teklif etti' gibi fiiller -eceğine / -meyi ile kurulur; İngilizcede hepsi aynı: + to + V1 (He promised to call me = Beni arayacağına söz verdi).
examples: We plan to visit our grandparents.
I managed to catch the bus.
He promised to call me.
She refused to accept the offer.

grammar.title: Zor olanlar: help (to), would like to, can't afford to, forget / remember
grammar.summary: help: to olabilir de olmayabilir de; ikisi de doğru: She helps me to understand = She helps me understand. Ama -ing olmaz (helps me studying ❌). would like to = want to'nun kibar hali (I would like to order a coffee; konuşmada I'd like to). 'I would like visit' ❌, to şart. afford genelde can / can't ile kullanılır: I can't afford to rent this apartment (Bu daireyi kiralamaya gücüm yetmiyor). I don't afford ❌. forget to / remember to = yapılacak bir işi unutmak / unutmamak. Türkçede ikisi de çoğu zaman 'unutma' diye çevrilir: Remember to turn off the lights = Don't forget to turn off the lights = Işıkları kapatmayı unutma. (forget / remember + V-ing farklı anlamdadır, 'geçmişte yaptığını hatırlamak'; bu aşamada sadece to'lu halini kullan.) try to = -meye çalışmak: I try to eat healthy food. prefer to + V1 (15. aşama): She prefers to work alone.
examples: Can you help me prepare dinner?
I would like to order a coffee.
I can't afford to rent this apartment.
Don't forget to take your medicine.

grammar.title: Senin cümlen: bir cümlede üç tane to
grammar.summary: Derste yazdığın cümle çok iyi: 'I decided to visit my parents because I wanted to help them to clean the house.' decided to visit, wanted to help, help them to clean: üç fiil, üçü de to + V1. help'ten sonra to atılabilir: ... I wanted to help them clean the house da doğru, hatta konuşmada daha yaygın. Tek düzeltme yazımda: cümleyi 'i decided' diye başlatmışsın; İngilizcede 'ben' her zaman büyük ve noktasız I (cümle ortasında bile: because I wanted). Kendi cümleni kurarken şunu sor: 'İlk fiil çekimlendi mi? (decided, wanted) to'dan sonraki fiil yalın mı? (visit, help, clean)'.
examples: I decided to visit my parents because I wanted to help them to clean the house.
I decided to visit my parents because I wanted to help them clean the house.

stories.title: Leo and the Blue Door
pages: Leo was ten years old, and he was [[curious|meraklı]] about everything. Why is the sky blue? Where do birds sleep? He asked a hundred questions every day. His grandmother always smiled and said, “Curious minds find [[hidden|gizli, saklı]] doors.” Leo didn't understand her. Not yet.

One rainy afternoon, he was [[alone|yalnız, tek başına]] in her old house. Suddenly, he heard a [[strange|garip, tuhaf]] [[noise|ses, gürültü]] behind the big clock in the hall. Tick, tock… knock, knock! Leo was a little afraid, but he wanted to know more. He [[pushed|itti]] the clock, and it moved. Behind it, there was a small blue door.

Leo opened the door and [[stepped|adım attı]] inside. He [[couldn't believe his eyes|gözlerine inanamadı]]. The trees were purple, the rivers were made of light, and tiny fish were [[floating|süzülüyordu]] in the air. A talking fox [[appeared|belirdi, ortaya çıktı]] and said, “Welcome, [[explorer|kâşif]]! Nobody has visited this world for fifty years.”

The fox showed him [[amazing|inanılmaz, harika]] places: a mountain that sang and a library with books that could talk. Leo asked questions all day, and every question opened a new door. When the clock [[struck|(saat) çaldı, vurdu]] eight, he ran home. “Grandma,” he [[whispered|fısıldadı]], “you were right.” She [[winked|göz kırptı]]. “I know. I found that door when I was a child, too.”

stories.title: Mira and the Grey Town
stories.titleTr: Renkleri gören Mira ve gri kasaba
pages: In the town of Greyford, everything was grey: the houses, the sky, the flowers, even people's clothes. Nobody [[noticed|fark etti]] it, because they [[had never seen|hiç görmemişlerdi]] anything different. But Mira was special. When she looked at an apple, she saw red. When she looked at the sea, she saw blue.

She told her friends, “The sky is blue! The grass is green!” They [[laughed at|(alay ederek) güldüler]] her. “You're [[imagining|hayal ediyorsun]] things,” they said. Mira felt sad and [[lonely|yalnız, kimsesiz]]. But one night, she found an old box of paints in the [[attic|çatı katı]]. The colors inside were [[bright|parlak, canlı]] and alive.

The next morning, Mira [[decided|karar verdi]] to show everyone what she could see. She painted a yellow sun on the school wall and red flowers on the old bridge. People stopped and [[stared|dik dik baktı]]. An old man touched the flowers and started to cry. “I remember this color,” he said. “I used to see it when I was young.”

[[Day by day|Günden güne]], the town changed. Children painted their doors, and the baker [[decorated|süsledi]] his shop with orange and pink. Soon, everyone could see colors again. The [[mayor|belediye başkanı]] gave Mira a small [[medal|madalya]] and asked, “How did you do it?” Mira smiled. “I didn't [[create|yaratmak, oluşturmak]] the colors. They were always here. I just helped you see them.”

stories.title: Nilo, the Invisible Ghost
pages: Nilo was an [[invisible|görünmez]] ghost. He lived in an old [[lighthouse|deniz feneri]] by the sea. Once, he could laugh, cry and feel everything. But one [[stormy|fırtınalı]] night, the wind [[blew away|uçurup götürdü]] all his feelings. Now he felt nothing at all. Not happy, not sad, just [[empty|boş]].

So Nilo [[went on a journey|yolculuğa çıktı]] to find them. In a busy market, he found Joy. It was hiding in a little girl's laugh as she [[chased|kovaladı]] a red balloon. Nilo touched the laugh, and suddenly he smiled. “One feeling back,” he thought. “Only a few more to go.”

In a hospital, he found Sadness. It was sitting next to an old woman who [[missed|özlüyordu]] her husband. Nilo didn't want it, but he took it [[gently|nazikçe]]. He cried for the first time in years. It hurt, but it was real. Then, on a dark bridge, he found Fear, [[shaking|titreyen]] like a small bird.

Nilo was afraid of Fear, but he held it [[anyway|yine de]]. Now he had Joy, Sadness and Fear, but something was still [[missing|eksik]]. Tired, he went back to the lighthouse. There, a lost kitten was crying in the rain. Nilo [[wrapped|sardı]] it in an old blanket, and a warm feeling [[filled|doldurdu]] his heart. It was Love, the last and the strongest feeling. It had never left him. It was only waiting. That night, for the first time, someone could see Nilo: the little kitten.

stories.title: Lumi, the Stranger in the Blue House
stories.titleTr: Doğduğu evde yabancı gibi hisseden Lumi
pages: Lumi was born in a small blue house at the end of a quiet street. But from the beginning, Lumi felt like a [[stranger|yabancı]]. Nobody in the house could see it. The family talked, ate and laughed, and Lumi only watched from the [[stairs|merdivenler]]. “Do I [[belong|ait olmak]] here?” it thought. “I'm not sure.”

As Lumi [[grew up|büyüdü]], it started to collect feelings. Every morning, it [[picked up|topladı]] little ones from the floor: the [[excitement|heyecan]] of the boy before school, the [[worry|endişe]] of the mother at the window. Lumi kept them in an old jar. At night, it opened the jar and felt them [[one by one|teker teker]].

But the feelings were not quiet. They always wanted to go somewhere. So Lumi [[followed|takip etti]] them. Excitement took it to the garden, where the boy was [[planting|dikiyordu]] his first tree. Worry took it to a dark room, where the grandfather couldn't sleep. Lumi sat next to him until the morning. “I can't fix it,” Lumi thought, “but I can stay.”

Day by day, something changed. Lumi's hands were not [[see-through|şeffaf]] anymore. They were soft and grey, like morning [[fog|sis]]. One evening, the little boy looked at the stairs and smiled. “Hi! You seem new here.” Lumi [[blushed|kızardı]]. “I'm the oldest one here,” it thought. Every feeling it [[carried|taşıdı]] made it a little more real. Now Lumi knew: you don't find a home. You slowly [[become part of|bir yerin parçası olmak]] it.

stories.title: Velmora Saga, Part 1: The Warrior Who Never Gave Up
stories.titleTr: Velmora Destanı, 1. Bölüm: Asla pes etmeyen savaşçı
pages: In the world of Velmora, every warrior was born in the same place: a small village called Thornwick. Kael Ironstep opened his eyes there one morning, with a wooden sword and nothing else. Above his head [[floated|havada süzülüyordu]] a name in white letters: DUSK_77. Kael didn't know what it meant. He only knew one thing. Something moved his legs, chose his words and [[made decisions|kararlar verdi]] for him. He called it “the Hand.” And the Hand had one goal: to reach the top of the [[Tower of the Ninth Crown|Dokuzuncu Taç Kulesi]] and [[beat the game|oyunu bitirmek, yenmek]].

His first fight was in Hollowdeep, a dark cave under the village. There, on a broken throne, sat the [[Hollow King|Kof Kral]], a small skeleton with a rusty crown. Every new player defeated him. It was [[a piece of cake|çok kolay]]. Kael hit him once, twice, three times. The king fell to his knees. Then something strange happened. Before the last hit, Kael's arm stopped in the air for one second. Nobody moved it. The king looked up with empty eyes and [[whispered|fısıldadı]], “You [[waited|bekledin]]. Interesting. See you again, little warrior.”

After Hollowdeep, the Hand took Kael everywhere. He fought rats, then wolves, then bandits in the forest. He died many times, but he always came back at the village fountain. Slowly, he [[got used to|alıştı]] the pain and the long walks. He [[made progress|ilerleme kaydetti]] every day: level 10, level 20, level 30. Kael was [[proud of|-den gurur duyuyordu]] every new scar. He used to be afraid of the Greyfang wolves. Now they ran away from him. But at night, he often saw a [[pale owl|solgun, beyaz bir baykuş]] in a tree. It was always watching him.

Then came Grommark, the Stone Giant of the northern hills. He was as tall as a castle, and his [[fists|yumruklar]] could break mountains. Kael attacked him and died in ten seconds. He tried again. And again. On the fiftieth try, he lost his sword. On the hundredth, he lost his hope. “[[Give up|pes et]],” a voice said in his head. “Find an easier way.” But Kael [[would rather|-meyi tercih ederdi]] die a thousand times than run away. He stood up, cleaned the mud from his face, and [[carried on|devam etti]].

So he stopped fighting for a while and started watching. He sat on a rock and [[paid attention to|-e dikkat etti]] every move of the giant. Grommark always raised his left foot before a big attack. He always [[roared|kükredi]] twice before he threw a rock. And after every third attack, he took a short break to breathe. Kael smiled. “I've [[figured it out|çözdüm, anladım]],” he said. On the three hundred and twelfth try, he waited for the break, ran between the giant's legs and hit the [[weak spot|zayıf nokta]] on his back.

The giant fell like a mountain, and the whole valley [[shook|sarsıldı]]. Players from everywhere came to see the warrior who never gave up. Some of them asked Kael to join their [[guilds|loncalar]]. “We're going to the Frost Lake tomorrow. [[Are you in?|Var mısın?]]” But the Hand always said no. Kael preferred to travel alone. Or maybe the Hand preferred it. He couldn't tell the difference anymore. Sometimes he wanted to stop and look at the sunset, and his feet stopped. Sometimes he wanted to talk, and his mouth spoke. That [[seemed|gibi görünüyordu]] strange. Was it the Hand, or was it him?

The road to the Tower went through the Ashen Wastes, a grey desert where nothing grew. There, Kael [[came across|rastladı, karşılaştı]] the frost dragon Vyrrath, the oldest creature in Velmora. Her wings covered the sun, and her breath turned the sand into ice. Kael's armor broke. His health went down to one point. He could [[hardly|zar zor, neredeyse hiç]] breathe. But he remembered the giant. Watch. Wait. Learn. When the dragon opened her mouth for the final attack, Kael threw his last [[torch|meşale]] into it. The ice inside her [[exploded|patladı]].

Finally, Kael stood in front of the Tower of the Ninth Crown. It was black and endless, and its top was lost in the clouds. He climbed for three days. On every floor, a new enemy was waiting: knights of shadow, iron spiders, a mirror that fought with his own moves. Kael [[went through|-den geçti, atlattı]] all of them. He didn't sleep. He didn't eat. He only had one thought: the top. “Almost there,” he told himself. “I can [[make it|başarabilirim]].” At the last door, the pale owl was sitting and waiting for him, [[as if|sanki ...-mış gibi]] it knew something.

Behind the door, there was no final boss. There was no treasure and no music. There was only a quiet room and a [[glowing|parıldayan]] stone in the middle. Kael touched it, and white letters appeared in the air: “PLAYER DUSK_77 – LAST LOGIN: 214 DAYS AGO.” Kael read it again and again. His hands began to [[shake|titremek]]. Two hundred and fourteen days. The giant, the dragon, the tower… [[In other words|başka bir deyişle]], the Hand wasn't there for any of it. Then a second line appeared under the first one, and Kael [[held his breath|nefesini tuttu]].

“TOTAL TIME PLAYED: 9 MINUTES.” Kael sat down on the cold floor. Nine minutes. The player left Velmora in the cave of the Hollow King, at the [[exact|tam, kesin]] second Kael's arm stopped in the air. Every fight after that, every choice, every [[step of the way|yolun her adımı]], was his own. Kael had always [[looked for|aradı]] the Hand. Now he finally [[found out|öğrendi, keşfetti]] the truth: there was no Hand. There was only Kael. Outside, the pale owl flew away into the night. And far away, a creature with a rusty crown looked up at the tower and smiled.

stories.title: Velmora Saga, Part 2: The Healer Who Asked Why
stories.titleTr: Velmora Destanı, 2. Bölüm: “Neden?” diye soran şifacı
pages: In the village of Thornwick, next to the fountain, there was a small white house with a green door. Inside lived Lira, the healer. All day, tired players came to her with broken bones and [[poisoned|zehirlenmiş]] blood. She was always [[swamped|işten başını kaldıramayan]]. She put her hands on each player and said the same words: “Rest, traveler. The light will [[carry|taşımak]] you.” She had said these words more than a million times. She was [[used to|alışkın]] it. She never asked why. She was an [[NPC|oyuncu olmayan karakter]], and NPCs didn't ask questions.

Then one evening, a strange player came in. She wasn't hurt. She just sat down and looked at Lira for a long time. Above her head, small white letters said: DUSK_77. “Can I ask you something?” the player said. “What do you want, Lira?” Lira opened her mouth. “Rest, traveler. The light will carry you.” “No,” the player said [[gently|nazikçe]]. “Not your [[line|replik, ezber cümle]]. What do you want?” Lira [[froze|donup kaldı]]. There was no answer inside her, only a strange, empty feeling, like a room without furniture. The player smiled sadly and left. Lira never saw her again.

That night, at midnight, the Silence came. It came every night. The wind stopped, the birds stopped, the fire stopped, and for one second the whole world [[held its breath|nefesini tuttu]]. After the Silence, NPCs forgot everything from the day before. But this time, Lira was [[afraid of forgetting|unutmaktan korkuyordu]] the question. So, before midnight, she [[came up with|(fikir) buldu]] a plan. She took a healing [[scroll|parşömen, tomar]] and wrote on it: “What do you want? Find out.” Then she hid it under her bed and waited for the dark.

In the morning, she found the scroll and didn't [[recognize|tanımak]] her own [[handwriting|el yazısı]]. But she read the words, and the empty feeling came back. From that day, she wrote a new scroll every night. Slowly, she started to [[notice|fark etmek]] things. The baker told the same joke every morning. The guard walked the same twenty steps, left and right, forever. Even the birds sang the same song. “Are we all [[asleep|uykuda]]?” she wondered. One night, she counted the scrolls under her bed. There were not twenty, not fifty. There were two hundred.

Lira [[made a decision|bir karar verdi]]. She wanted to see the world outside Thornwick. But NPCs couldn't leave their villages. At the end of the road, there was an [[invisible wall|görünmez duvar]]. Every time she walked into it, she woke up next to the fountain. She tried a hundred times. Then she [[took advantage of|-den faydalandı, fırsat bildi]] the Silence. At midnight, when the world stopped, the wall stopped too, just for one second. Lira ran. When the world started again, she was on the other side, and her heart was [[beating|çarpıyordu]] like a drum.

Outside, Velmora was beautiful and cruel. She saw forests full of silver leaves and rivers that sang. She also saw players who hurt monsters for fun and left them [[bleeding|kanlar içinde]] on the road. A small grey wolf [[cried|inledi]] under a tree, with an arrow in his leg. Lira stopped. She used to believe that healers were only for players. That was the rule. But she knelt down, pulled out the arrow and [[looked after|-e baktı, ilgilendi]] the wolf all night. In the morning, he licked her hand and ran into the forest. Lira felt useful, because this time she chose it.

She walked for many days and asked everyone the same question. “What do you want?” A knight said, “I want to [[take part in|-e katılmak]] every battle.” A [[merchant|tüccar]] said, “Gold, of course!” An old lamplighter said, “[[I'm torn|iki arada kaldım]]. I'd like to rest, but I'd rather keep the lamps on for travelers.” Lira liked his answer. “Do you remember yesterday?” she asked him. The old man laughed. “Nobody remembers, dear. But they say there is a place at the end of the world where you can read the [[gods' writing|tanrıların yazısı]]. They call it the Seam.”

The Seam was a long [[crack|çatlak, yarık]] in the sky above the Ashen Wastes. Through it, Lira saw a strange world of numbers and light. Lines of white words moved slowly in the dark, like fish in deep water. She couldn't understand most of them. But one message was clear, and it [[made her blood run cold|kanını dondurdu]]: “VELMORA WILL CLOSE FOREVER AT MIDNIGHT ON THE LAST DAY OF WINTER. THANK YOU FOR PLAYING.” Lira [[stepped back|geri çekildi]]. Forever. The wolf, the lamplighter, the baker's joke, her scrolls. Everything was going to [[disappear|yok olmak]].

She sat on the grey sand and cried for the first time. What was [[the point of|...-in anlamı, faydası]] wanting something, if everything was going to end? Then she remembered her scrolls. She took the newest one out of her bag. Under the question, there was a line she didn't remember writing. Maybe she wrote it after the Silence, half asleep. It said: “You don't need forever to [[make a difference|fark yaratmak]]. You only need today.” Lira read it twice. Then she [[wiped|sildi]] her tears, stood up and [[looked around|etrafına bakındı]].

Not far from the Seam, someone was sitting alone on a rock. It was a warrior with a broken sword and a tired face. Above his head, white letters said: DUSK_77. Lira's [[heart jumped|kalbi hop etti]]. It was the same name she saw above the strange player's head, long ago. But this one was different. His eyes were [[alive|canlı]]. To [[break the ice|buzları eritmek, sohbeti başlatmak]], she asked, “Are you hurt?” The warrior laughed quietly. “Not my body. I just [[found out|öğrendim]] that nobody controls me. So… what am I for?” Lira sat down next to him. “I've asked a question like that for two hundred and fourteen nights,” she said. “Let's find out together.”

stories.title: Velmora Saga, Part 3: The Rise of the Hollow King
stories.titleTr: Velmora Destanı, 3. Bölüm: Kof Kral'ın yükselişi
pages: Deep under Thornwick, in the cave of Hollowdeep, sat Morvane, the Hollow King. He was the first boss of Velmora, and the weakest. His crown was [[rusty|paslı]], his bones were [[thin|ince]], and his sword was made of wood. Every new player came to his cave, hit him three times and laughed. “Easy boss. [[A piece of cake|Çok kolay]].” Morvane fell, the player got a small [[reward|ödül]], and a minute later the king sat on his throne again, waiting for the next one. He had died more than a million times. Nobody ever remembered his name.

Morvane used to [[accept|kabullenmek]] his life. Die, wake up, die again. It was simple. Then one day, something different happened. A young warrior came in, with the name DUSK_77 above his head. He hit the king once, twice, three times, like everybody. But before the last hit, his arm stopped. Just for one second, the warrior [[hesitated|tereddüt etti]]. Nobody had ever done that. In that second, Morvane looked into the warrior's eyes and saw something [[impossible|imkânsız]]: [[a choice|bir seçim]]. “You waited,” the king whispered. “Interesting.” Then the sword fell, and everything went dark.

That night, the Silence came. The whole world stopped and forgot. But Morvane didn't forget. He woke up on his throne and remembered everything: the warrior, the waiting, the choice. And for the first time, he remembered all his deaths, too. A million swords. A million laughs. He [[couldn't stand|dayanamadı]] it anymore. He stood up, and his empty eyes began to [[burn|yanmak]] with green fire. “No more,” he said to the dark. “I'm [[fed up with|-den bıktım]] dying. [[From now on|bundan sonra]], I will be the one who wins.”

But how could the weakest boss become strong? Morvane [[thought it over|üzerinde uzun uzun düşündü]] for many nights. Then he [[figured out|çözdü, anladı]] a secret of Velmora. When a player killed a monster, the player took its power. Why couldn't a monster do the same? He [[set a goal|bir hedef koydu]]: he would defeat every creature in Velmora, one by one, and take all their power. Then he would become the greatest boss the world had ever seen. He left his cave for the first time in his life. Outside, the moon was full, and the wolves were [[howling|uluyordu]].

The Greyfang wolves were his first [[victims|kurbanlar]]. They were fast and hungry, and they came at him from every side. Morvane fell many times. But dying was the one thing he was [[good at|-de iyi, usta]]. He came back again and again, and every time he learned something. After a week, the wolf king lay at his feet. Morvane put his hand on the wolf's head and [[absorbed|emdi, içine çekti]] his speed. And this time, the wolf didn't come back. Next was Old Nettle, the swamp witch. He took her poison. Then the bandit lord of the forest. He took his [[cunning|kurnazlık]].

Then he climbed the northern hills to [[deal with|-in hakkından gelmek]] Grommark, the Stone Giant. The giant laughed. “You? The little tutorial king?” Morvane didn't answer. He already knew the giant's secret. He had watched [[a certain|belli bir]] warrior fight him for weeks. Raise the left foot. Roar twice. Take a break after the third attack. Morvane waited for the break and hit the weak spot. When Grommark fell, the king took his strength. Now he was taller than a house. Monsters began to whisper his name [[in fear|korkuyla]]. Some hid in caves. Others [[bowed down|eğildi, boyun eğdi]] before him.

Not every monster was afraid of him. Vyrrath, the frost dragon, waited for him in the Ashen Wastes. She was old and [[wise|bilge]], and her eyes were full of sadness. “I know what you are doing,” she said. “But power won't [[fill|doldurmak]] the hole inside you.” “I'd rather be [[feared|korkulan]] than forgotten,” Morvane answered. The battle [[lasted|sürdü]] three days and three nights. The sand turned to ice, and the ice turned to fire. In the end, the dragon fell. With her last breath, she said, “Look up at the Seam, little king. Then you will understand.”

Morvane looked up. Above the desert, there was a long [[crack|çatlak]] in the sky, and white words were moving inside it. He read the message slowly: “VELMORA WILL CLOSE FOREVER AT MIDNIGHT ON THE LAST DAY OF WINTER.” Below it, there was another line, smaller and [[almost hidden|neredeyse gizli]]: “[[BACKUP|YEDEK]]: THE FINAL BOSS WILL BE SAVED FOR THE NEXT WORLD…” Morvane didn't read the rest. His green eyes burned brighter. So that was it. When the world ended, only one creature would [[survive|hayatta kalmak]]. Not the strongest player. Not the kindest healer. The final boss. He smiled for the first time in a million deaths.

He went to the Tower of the Ninth Crown and climbed it in one night. The shadow knights, the iron spiders, the mirror: none of them could stop him. At the top, he found a quiet room, a [[glowing|parıldayan]] stone and an empty floor. There was no final boss. The gods had never finished the game. Morvane laughed, and the tower shook. “Then I will be it,” he said. He [[built|yaptı, inşa etti]] a throne from the bones of the monsters he had defeated, and he sat down on it. The game [[accepted|kabul etti]] him. Above his head, red letters appeared: FINAL BOSS.

But the game wasn't finished with him. A small message appeared: “CREATURES [[REMAINING|KALAN]]: 2.” Morvane [[frowned|kaşlarını çattı]]. He had defeated every monster in Velmora. Every wolf, every witch, every giant. Who was left? He touched the glowing stone, and it showed him two faces. The first was a warrior with a broken sword, the same warrior who once waited before the last hit. The second was a healer from Thornwick with a bag full of scrolls. Morvane [[leaned back|arkasına yaslandı]] on his throne of bones. “Well, well,” he whispered. “See you again, little warrior.” Outside, winter was [[coming to an end|sona eriyordu]].

stories.title: Velmora Saga, Part 4: The Last Night of Winter
stories.titleTr: Velmora Destanı, 4. Bölüm: Kışın son gecesi
pages: It was the last day of winter. In a few hours, at midnight, Velmora would close forever. The sky was turning red, and the ground [[trembled|titriyordu]]. There were no monsters left in the forests, no wolves on the hills, no dragon in the desert. Only silence. Kael and Lira stood in front of the Tower of the Ninth Crown. They had [[traveled together|birlikte yolculuk etmişlerdi]] for weeks. He had learned to listen. She had learned to fight. “Are you afraid?” Kael asked. “Yes,” Lira said. “But I'd rather be afraid with you than [[safe|güvende]] without you.”

At the door of the tower, the pale owl was waiting again. This time, it didn't fly away. It [[followed|takip etti]] them up the stairs, floor after floor. The tower was empty. The shadow knights and iron spiders were gone. Morvane had taken them all. “He isn't just strong,” Kael said. “He's every monster we have ever met.” Lira [[nodded|başını salladı]]. She had a bag of healing potions and all her old scrolls. “[[Keep in mind|Aklında bulunsun]],” she said, “I can heal you, but I can't bring you back. Tonight, if we die, we won't [[respawn|yeniden doğmak]].”

At the top, the room wasn't quiet anymore. A huge throne of bones stood in the middle, and on it sat Morvane, the Hollow King. He wasn't small now. He was as tall as the giant, he had the dragon's [[wings|kanatlar]], and his eyes burned with green fire. Above his head, red letters said: FINAL BOSS. “Welcome, little warrior,” he said. “I've been [[looking forward to|dört gözle bekliyordum]] seeing you again. You were the first one who waited. Now you will be the last one who [[falls|düşer, yenilir]].” He stood up, and the whole tower [[shook|sarsıldı]].

The battle began. Morvane attacked with the giant's fists, the witch's poison and the wolves' speed. Kael [[blocked|engelledi, savuşturdu]] and jumped and rolled, but every hit pushed him back. In the first minute, his shield broke. In the second, his armor [[cracked|çatladı]]. Lira stood behind him and kept him alive, spell after spell, potion after potion. “I can't hit him!” Kael shouted. “He's too fast!” Morvane laughed. “You used to beat monsters one by one. But you can't beat all of them [[at once|aynı anda]]. [[Give up|Pes et]], warrior. It's over.”

Kael fell to one knee. His health was very low. Then he remembered Grommark and the three hundred tries. Watch. Wait. Learn. He stopped attacking and started to [[observe|gözlemlemek]]. And slowly, he saw it. Every time before a big attack, Morvane raised his right arm and took three small steps back. It was the old move of the tutorial king, the little skeleton in Hollowdeep. Morvane had taken a thousand powers, but he couldn't [[get rid of|-den kurtulmak]] his oldest [[habit|alışkanlık]]. “Lira,” Kael whispered, “I've [[figured him out|onu çözdüm]].”

The next time the king raised his arm, Kael didn't step back. He ran forward, under the arm, and hit Morvane's crown with all his strength. The crown cracked. A wolf's [[howl|uluma]] came out of it, then the cry of a dragon. Morvane screamed. “No! They're mine!” He hit Kael with a giant fist, and the warrior flew across the room and [[crashed into|-e çarptı]] the wall. He didn't move. Lira ran to him. His health was almost zero, but his heart was still beating, very slowly. She had only one spell left, [[only enough|ancak yetecek kadar]] for one person.

Lira looked at Kael. Then she looked at Morvane. The king was [[holding|tutuyordu]] his broken crown, and behind the fire in his eyes, she saw something she knew very well. It was fear. The same fear she had felt at the Seam. Healers are only for players. That used to be the rule. But Lira had made her own rules a long time ago. She thought of the little wolf with the arrow in his leg. Then she [[made the hardest decision|en zor kararı verdi]] of her life. She [[turned away from|-den yüz çevirdi]] Kael, walked to the Hollow King and put her hands on his crown.

“Rest, traveler,” she whispered. “The light will carry you.” For the first time in a million times, the words meant something. Green light filled the room. The crack in the crown opened wide, and every creature Morvane had taken flew out of it: wolves, spiders, knights, the witch, the giant, the dragon. They were free. A small grey wolf with a [[scar|yara izi]] on his leg ran to Kael and licked his face. Kael [[coughed|öksürdü]] and opened his eyes. “Next time you want to fight a final boss,” he said weakly, “[[count me out|beni saymayın, ben yokum]].” On the throne, there was only a little skeleton now, [[shaking|titreyen]] like a child.

“Why did you do that?” Morvane asked Lira. “I wanted to [[survive|hayatta kalmak]]. When the world ends, only the final boss will be saved. I'd rather be a monster forever than nothing.” Then the pale owl landed on the glowing stone. Its [[feathers|tüyler]] turned to light, and a woman's voice filled the room. “That's not what the message says, Morvane. You didn't read it to the end.” Above her, white letters appeared: DUSK_77. Kael [[stared|gözlerini dikip baktı]]. “You… you're the Hand.” “No,” she said. “I made this world. And I [[let go of|bıraktım]] you after nine minutes, so you could choose.”

She touched the stone, and the full message appeared: “BACKUP: THE FINAL BOSS WILL BE SAVED FOR THE NEXT WORLD, WITH EVERY CHARACTER WHO STANDS BY ITS SIDE.” “A boss alone is just a monster,” DUSK_77 said. “A boss with friends is a story.” Morvane looked at Kael. Kael looked at Lira. Lira [[held out|uzattı]] her hand. [[One by one|Birer birer]], they all stepped onto the stone: a warrior who never gave up, a healer who chose her meaning, a small king who was tired of being alone, and every free creature behind them. The clock [[struck|vurdu, çaldı]] midnight. The world went dark. And somewhere, on a new server, their names [[began to glow|parlamaya başladı]].

homework.title: B1 Collocations + günlük ifadeler 1
homework.note: Her gün birkaç ifade, salı günü konuşurken hepsi dilinin ucunda olacak!

items.tip: 'do a decision' değil, her zaman 'make'. Geçmiş: made a decision. make a decision to + fiil.

ex.en: She [[made a decision]] to move abroad.
I can't [[make a decision]] right now.
We need to [[make a decision]] before Friday.
My brother is [[making a decision]] about his job.
ex.tr: Kardeşim işiyle ilgili bir karar veriyor.

ex.en: Did you [[make a decision]] about the holiday?

items.tip: take a look at + şey. Geçmiş: took a look. 'have a look' da aynı anlam.

ex.en: Let's [[take a look]] at this.
Can you [[take a look]] at my homework?
I [[took a look]] at the new menu yesterday.
ex.tr: Dün yeni menüye bir göz attım.

ex.en: The mechanic will [[take a look]] at my car.
She is [[taking a look]] at the map now.

items.tip: keep in mind that + cümle ya da keep sth in mind. Geçmiş: kept in mind.

ex.en: Please [[keep in mind]] to bring your ID.
[[Keep in mind]] that the shop closes at six.
I always [[keep in mind]] my teacher's advice.
We should [[keep in mind]] the weather for the trip.
ex.tr: Gezi için havayı göz önünde bulundurmalıyız.

ex.en: She [[kept in mind]] everything you told her.
ex.tr: Ona söylediğin her şeyi aklında tuttu.

items.tip: Düzensiz: bring - brought - brought. Ayrılabilir: bring it up (zamir ortaya girer).

ex.en: He [[brought up]] the problem in the meeting.
She [[brought up]] the idea at dinner.
ex.tr: Akşam yemeğinde bu fikri ortaya attı.

ex.en: Don't [[bring up]] politics with my uncle!
I will [[bring up]] this question in class.
Why do you always [[bring up]] money?

items.tip: Giyme hareketi (wear = giymiş olmak). Düzensiz: put - put - put. Zamirle: put it on.

ex.en: She [[put on]] her coat and left.
[[Put on]] your shoes, we're late!
I'm [[putting on]] a warm sweater today.
My dad always [[puts on]] his glasses to read.
ex.tr: Babam okumak için hep gözlüğünü takar.

ex.en: You should [[put on]] a hat in the sun.

items.tip: take part in + isim / -ing. Geçmiş: took part in. 'join' ile yakın anlam.

ex.en: I [[took part in]] the competition last year.
All students should [[take part in]] the project.
My sister is [[taking part in]] a dance show.
ex.tr: Kız kardeşim bir dans gösterisine katılıyor.

ex.en: We will [[take part in]] the online tournament.
Do you want to [[take part in]] the meeting?

items.tip: Ayrılmaz: come across sth. Düzensiz: come - came - come.

ex.en: I [[came across]] an old photo in the box.
She [[came across]] a nice café downtown.
ex.tr: Şehir merkezinde güzel bir kafeye rastladı.

ex.en: You often [[come across]] this word in books.
Did you [[come across]] my keys anywhere?
We [[came across]] an old friend at the airport.

items.tip: Ayrılmaz: look after sb/sth. Düzenli: looked after. 'take care of' ile eş anlamlı.

ex.en: She [[looks after]] her younger brother.
Can you [[look after]] my cat this weekend?
ex.tr: Bu hafta sonu kedime bakabilir misin?

ex.en: My grandmother [[looked after]] me as a child.
I'm [[looking after]] the plants while they're away.
You should [[look after]] your health.

items.tip: Düzensiz: find - found - found. find out that / find out what, where...

ex.en: I [[found out]] the truth yesterday.
Let's [[find out]] what time the film starts.
She will [[find out]] about the party soon.
How did you [[find out]] my address?
We are trying to [[find out]] the problem.

items.tip: get used to + isim / -ing (to'dan sonra fiil+ing!). Geçmiş: got used to.

ex.en: She's [[getting used to]] the new place.
I can't [[get used to]] waking up early.
My brother [[got used to]] the cold weather.
You will [[get used to]] the new job.
It's hard to [[get used to]] a new language.

items.tip: Düzensiz: deal - dealt - dealt. deal with + sorun/kişi.

ex.en: I don't know how to [[deal with]] stress.
The manager [[dealt with]] the problem quickly.
She [[deals with]] angry customers every day.
We will [[deal with]] this tomorrow.
Can you [[deal with]] the emails, please?

items.tip: Her zaman 'on' ile: depend on (from değil!). It depends on... = ...e bağlı.

ex.en: You can [[depend on]] me.
Our plans [[depend on]] the weather.
The kids still [[depend on]] their parents.
I [[depended on]] my friends during exams.
The price [[depends on]] the size.

items.tip: be proud of + isim / -ing. 'with' değil 'of'. am/is/are/was proud of.

ex.en: She [[is proud of]] her achievements.
I [[am proud of]] you!
My parents [[were proud of]] my exam results.
We [[are proud of]] our team.
He [[was proud of]] finishing the marathon.

items.mean: use something in a good way
items.tip: İki anlam: fırsattan yararlanmak (+) veya birini kullanmak (-). Geçmiş: took advantage of.

ex.en: Don't [[take advantage of]] their kindness.
I [[took advantage of]] the sale and bought shoes.
You should [[take advantage of]] this chance.
We are [[taking advantage of]] the sunny weather.
She [[takes advantage of]] free English lessons online.

items.tip: Düzensiz: give - gave - given. give up + -ing (give up smoking). Zamirle: give it up.

ex.en: He [[gave up]] smoking last year.
Don't [[give up]], you can do it!
I never [[give up]] in difficult games.
She is going to [[give up]] sugar.
They [[gave up]] after three hours.

items.tip: 'do progress' değil 'make'. progress sayılamaz: 'a progress' yok. make progress in/with.

ex.en: She's [[making progress]] in English.
We [[made progress]] on the project today.
You will [[make progress]] if you practise.
My little brother [[makes progress]] every week.
I want to [[make progress]] with my speaking.

items.tip: İki anlam: sakinleşmek / evlenip düzen kurmak. Düzenli: settled down.

ex.en: After a long day, she [[settled down]] on the sofa.
ex.tr: Uzun bir günün ardından koltukta dinlendi.

ex.en: Please [[settle down]], the lesson is starting.
The baby [[settled down]] after his milk.
They want to [[settle down]] in a small town.
My cousin is going to [[settle down]] and get married.

items.tip: figure out + how/what/why... Düzenli: figured out. Zamirle: figure it out.

ex.en: I finally [[figured out]] the answer.
Can you [[figure out]] this puzzle?
We need to [[figure out]] how to get there.
She is trying to [[figure out]] the new phone.
I can't [[figure out]] why he is angry.

items.tip: carry on + -ing ya da carry on with + isim. Düzenli: carried on (y→ied).

ex.en: Let's [[carry on]] with the plan.
Please [[carry on]], I'm listening.
She [[carried on]] working after midnight.
ex.tr: Gece yarısından sonra da çalışmaya devam etti.

ex.en: We will [[carry on]] after a short break.
ex.tr: Kısa bir aradan sonra devam edeceğiz.

ex.en: They [[carry on]] playing even in the rain.

items.tip: be careful with + şey; be careful of = -den sakın. Emir: Be careful with...!

ex.en: [[Be careful with]] hot drinks.
You should [[be careful with]] your money.
My mom [[is careful with]] her new car.
ex.tr: Annem yeni arabasına çok özen gösteriyor.

ex.en: I [[was careful with]] the glasses, but one broke.
ex.tr: Bardaklara dikkat ettim ama biri kırıldı.

ex.en: Kids, [[be careful with]] the knife!

items.tip: keep in touch with + kişi. Geçmiş: kept in touch. 'stay in touch' da olur.

ex.en: Let's [[keep in touch]]!
I [[keep in touch]] with my school friends.
We [[kept in touch]] after the trip.
She will [[keep in touch]] by email.
It's hard to [[keep in touch]] when you're busy.

items.tip: take a break from + iş. Geçmiş: took a break. 'give a break' farklı anlam.

ex.en: I'm going to [[take a break]].
Let's [[take a break]] for ten minutes.
We [[took a break]] and had some tea.
You should [[take a break]] from your phone.
She is [[taking a break]] from work this week.

items.tip: Düzensiz: go - went - gone. Ayrıca 'gözden geçirmek' anlamı da var.

ex.en: She [[went through]] a tough time last year.
ex.tr: Geçen yıl zor bir dönem geçirdi.

ex.en: My family is [[going through]] some problems.
I don't want to [[go through]] that again.
We [[went through]] a lot together.
Many people [[go through]] stress before exams.
ex.tr: Birçok insan sınavlardan önce stres yaşar.

items.tip: Nesnesiz = spor yapmak. work sth out = çözmek. Düzenli: worked out.

ex.en: I [[work out]] three times a week.
She [[worked out]] at the gym this morning.
We're going to [[work out]] together tomorrow.
My brother is [[working out]] in his room.
Don't worry, everything will [[work out]].
ex.tr: Merak etme, her şey yoluna girecek.

items.tip: get along with + kişi. Geçmiş: got along with. 'get on with' (BrE) aynı anlam.

ex.en: She [[gets along with]] her colleagues.
I don't [[get along with]] my neighbour.
The two cats [[got along with]] each other quickly.
Do you [[get along with]] your sister?
He is easy to [[get along with]].

items.tip: take care of + kişi/şey. Geçmiş: took care of. Vedalaşırken: Take care!

ex.en: He [[takes care of]] his family.
Can you [[take care of]] the tickets?
I [[took care of]] my sick friend last week.
She is [[taking care of]] the baby today.
Don't worry, I'll [[take care of]] it.

items.tip: 'do a difference' değil 'make'. make a big/real difference. Geçmiş: made a difference.

ex.en: Small actions can [[make a difference]].
Teachers [[make a difference]] in our lives.
Your help really [[made a difference]].
I want to [[make a difference]] in my city.
Will this new rule [[make a difference]]?
ex.tr: Bu yeni kural bir fark yaratacak mı?

items.tip: come up with + idea/plan/solution. Düzensiz: came up with. Ayrılmaz.

ex.en: I [[came up with]] a great idea!
We need to [[come up with]] a plan.
She always [[comes up with]] funny names.
Can you [[come up with]] a better answer?
ex.tr: Daha iyi bir cevap bulabilir misin?

ex.en: They [[came up with]] a solution in one hour.

items.tip: to'dan sonra isim / -ing: look forward to seeing you (to see değil!).

ex.en: I'm [[looking forward to]] the holiday.
We [[look forward to]] seeing you soon.
ex.tr: Sizi yakında görmeyi dört gözle bekliyoruz.

ex.en: She is [[looking forward to]] her birthday party.
My kids always [[look forward to]] the weekend.
ex.tr: Çocuklarım hafta sonunu hep dört gözle bekler.

ex.en: I [[looked forward to]] this game for months.
ex.tr: Bu oyunu aylarca dört gözle bekledim.

items.tip: 'give attention' değil 'pay'. Düzensiz: pay - paid - paid. pay attention to + isim.

ex.en: Please [[pay attention to]] the instructions.
He didn't [[pay attention to]] the teacher.
You should [[pay attention to]] the road.
She [[paid attention to]] every detail.
Nobody is [[paying attention to]] me!

items.mean: decide what you want to achieve
items.tip: Düzensiz: set - set - set. set a goal (tekil) / set goals. 'put goals' değil.

ex.en: I want to [[set goals]] for my future.
We [[set goals]] at the start of every year.
My coach helped me [[set goals]].
You should [[set goals]] you can reach.
She is [[setting goals]] for her English.

items.tip: Gündelik dil. He's broke / We're broke. 'broken' değil, 'broke'!

ex.en: [[I'm broke]], so I can't come tonight.
ex.tr: Beş parasızım, o yüzden bu akşam gelemem.

ex.en: Sorry, [[I'm broke]] until payday.
ex.tr: Kusura bakma, maaş gününe kadar meteliğim yok.

ex.en: [[I'm broke]] after buying that new game.
ex.tr: O yeni oyunu aldıktan sonra beş parasız kaldım.

ex.en: Can you pay for lunch? [[I'm broke]].
ex.tr: Öğle yemeğini sen ödeyebilir misin? Beş parasızım.

ex.en: [[I'm broke]] this month, let's stay home.
ex.tr: Bu ay beş parasızım, evde kalalım.

items.tip: Samimi, arkadaşlar arası. Hit me up when/if... Resmî yazışmada kullanma.

ex.en: [[Hit me up]] when you get home.
[[Hit me up]] if you want to play tonight.
ex.tr: Bu akşam oynamak istersen bana yaz.

ex.en: I'm free tomorrow, [[hit me up]]!
[[Hit me up]] on WhatsApp later.
If you need help, just [[hit me up]].
ex.tr: Yardıma ihtiyacın olursa bana yazman yeter.

items.tip: Soruya cevap olarak: Beats me! diye kısaltılır. It beats me why/how...

ex.en: Where is Tom? [[It beats me]].
[[It beats me]] why she left so early.
ex.tr: Neden o kadar erken gittiğine dair hiçbir fikrim yok.

ex.en: [[It beats me]] how this machine works.
ex.tr: Bu makinenin nasıl çalıştığını hiç bilmiyorum.

ex.en: Why is the bus late? [[It beats me]]!
ex.tr: Otobüs neden geç kaldı? Hiç bilmiyorum!

ex.en: [[It beats me]] what the teacher wants.

items.mean: I'm tired of something and annoyed
items.tip: I'm fed up with + isim / -ing. She's fed up / We're fed up.

[[I'm fed up]] with waiting for the bus.
Stop it, [[I'm fed up]]!
[[I'm fed up]] with my noisy neighbours.
[[I'm fed up]], I need a holiday.

items.mean: I can't choose between two things
items.tip: I'm torn between A and B. 'torn' = tear (yırtmak) fiilinin V3'ü.

[[I'm torn]], both jobs look great.

ex.en: [[I'm torn]] about going to the party.
Honestly, [[I'm torn]] between these two phones.
ex.tr: Açıkçası bu iki telefon arasında kaldım.

ex.en: [[I'm torn]], should I stay or go?
ex.tr: İki arada kaldım, kalayım mı gideyim mi?

homework.title: Ability & Talent + günlük ifadeler 2

items.tip: have the ability to + fiil (yalın). 'can' anlamında ama daha resmi. Geçmiş: had the ability to.

ex.en: She [[has the ability to]] speak four languages.

ex.tr: Bazı kuşlar insan sesini taklit edebilir.

items.mean: let people see that you can do something well
items.tip: show ability in + isim/-ing. Genelde sıfatla: show great ability. Geçmiş: showed ability.

ex.en: He [[showed ability]] in maths at a young age.
The new player [[shows ability]] on the field.

ex.tr: Öğrenciler beceriyi birçok farklı yolla gösterebilir.

items.tip: have a natural ability to + fiil / for + isim. Öğrenilmemiş, kendiliğinden olan beceri.

ex.en: He has [[a natural talent]] for singing.
Her dancing comes from [[a natural talent]].
You don't need [[a natural talent]] to learn guitar.
ex.tr: Gitar öğrenmek için doğuştan yeteneğe ihtiyacın yok.

ex.en: My sister showed [[a natural talent]] for painting.
ex.tr: Kız kardeşim resme doğuştan yetenek gösterdi.

ex.en: Is it hard work or [[a natural talent]]?
ex.tr: Bu sıkı çalışma mı, doğuştan yetenek mi?

items.tip: Övgü için: You have a real talent! a real talent for + isim/-ing.

ex.en: You have [[a real talent]] for cooking!
ex.tr: Yemek yapmada gerçek bir yeteneğin var!

ex.en: That young actor is [[a real talent]].
ex.tr: O genç oyuncu gerçek bir yetenek.

ex.en: She has [[a real talent]] for making people relax.
ex.tr: İnsanları rahatlatmada gerçek bir yeteneği var.

ex.en: I think he has [[a real talent]] for writing.
ex.tr: Bence yazmaya gerçek bir yeteneği var.

ex.en: Our teacher said I had [[a real talent]].
ex.tr: Öğretmenimiz bende gerçek bir yetenek olduğunu söyledi.

items.mean: let people see your natural skill
items.tip: show talent for/in + isim. Sıfatla da olur: show real talent. Geçmiş: showed talent.

ex.en: He [[showed talent]] for music at age five.
Many kids [[show talent]] in art at school.
ex.tr: Birçok çocuk okulda sanatta yetenek gösterir.

ex.en: She is starting to [[show talent]] as a singer.
The team's new player [[shows talent]].
Did your son [[show talent]] for drawing early?
ex.tr: Oğlun resme erken yaşta yetenek gösterdi mi?

items.mean: find out that you are good at something
items.tip: discover a talent for + isim/-ing. Geçmiş: discovered a talent. Sık: discover a hidden talent.

ex.en: I [[discovered a talent]] for cooking last year.
ex.tr: Geçen yıl yemek yapma yeteneğimi keşfettim.

ex.en: She [[discovered a talent]] she never knew about.
You might [[discover a talent]] in this class.
He [[discovered a talent]] for acting at university.
Travelling helps people [[discover a talent]].
ex.tr: Seyahat etmek insanların bir yeteneğini keşfetmesine yardım eder.

items.tip: Yetenek doğuştan gelir ama çalışarak develop edilir. Geçmiş: developed a talent.

ex.en: Good teachers help students [[develop a talent]].
ex.tr: İyi öğretmenler öğrencilerin yeteneğini geliştirmesine yardım eder.

ex.en: She [[developed a talent]] for photography.
It takes years to [[develop a talent]].
He is [[developing a talent]] for public speaking.
You can't [[develop a talent]] without practice.

items.tip: Kişi için de kullanılır: She is a great talent. a great talent for + isim/-ing.

ex.en: He has [[a great talent]] for football.
Everyone says she is [[a great talent]].
ex.tr: Herkes onun büyük bir yetenek olduğunu söylüyor.

ex.en: My grandmother had [[a great talent]] for sewing.
ex.tr: Büyükannemin dikişe büyük bir yeteneği vardı.

ex.en: This band has [[a great talent]] on drums.
ex.tr: Bu grubun davulda büyük bir yeteneği var.

ex.en: You have [[a great talent]], so don't give up!
ex.tr: Büyük bir yeteneğin var, o yüzden pes etme!

items.mean: I'm in big trouble or very tired (slang)
items.tip: Gençlerin argosu. Başın dertteyken ya da çok yorgunken: I'm cooked. Resmi ortamda kullanma.

ex.en: I didn't study for the exam. [[I'm cooked]].
My boss saw me sleeping. [[I'm cooked]]!
ex.tr: Patronum beni uyurken gördü. İşim bitti!

ex.en: Ten hours of work today, [[I'm cooked]].
I lost my mom's keys. [[I'm cooked]]!
The deadline is tomorrow and [[I'm cooked]].
ex.tr: Son gün yarın ve işim bitti.

items.tip: Biri 'Sana bir şey anlatacağım' dediğinde: I'm all ears! Merakla dinlediğini gösterir.

ex.en: Tell me about your trip. [[I'm all ears]].
ex.tr: Bana geziyi anlat. Can kulağıyla dinliyorum.

ex.en: You have news? [[I'm all ears]]!
ex.tr: Haberin mi var? Can kulağıyla dinliyorum!

ex.en: If you have a better idea, [[I'm all ears]].
ex.tr: Daha iyi bir fikrin varsa, dinliyorum.

ex.en: Okay, [[I'm all ears]], what happened?
ex.tr: Tamam, can kulağıyla dinliyorum, ne oldu?

ex.en: Go on, [[I'm all ears]].

items.tip: Özür ya da teşekküre cevap: No big deal. Bir şeyi küçümsemek için: It's no big deal.

ex.en: You forgot my pen? [[No big deal]].
Thanks for the help! - [[No big deal]].
We missed the bus, but it's [[no big deal]].
Don't worry about the cup, [[no big deal]].
Being a bit late is [[no big deal]] here.
ex.tr: Burada biraz geç kalmak önemli değil.

items.tip: Küçük hatalar için kısa, samimi özür. Ciddi durumda 'I'm sorry, it was my fault' de.

ex.en: Oh, that was your seat? [[My bad]]!
ex.tr: Ah, orası senin yerin miydi? Benim hatam!

ex.en: [[My bad]], I sent the wrong file.
Sorry I'm late, [[my bad]].
ex.tr: Geç kaldığım için üzgünüm, benim hatam.

ex.en: I took your coffee by mistake. [[My bad]].
ex.tr: Yanlışlıkla senin kahveni aldım. Benim hatam.

ex.en: [[My bad]], I forgot to call you back.
ex.tr: Benim hatam, seni geri aramayı unuttum.

items.tip: Karşındakinin açıklamasını kabul ederken: Fair enough. Tam katılmasan da makul bulduğunu gösterir.

ex.en: I'm too tired to go out. - [[Fair enough]].
ex.tr: Dışarı çıkamayacak kadar yorgunum. - Tamam, mantıklı.

ex.en: [[Fair enough]], we can meet tomorrow then.
ex.tr: Tamam, mantıklı, o zaman yarın buluşuruz.

ex.en: He wants more money, and that's [[fair enough]].
ex.tr: Daha fazla para istiyor ve bu mantıklı.

ex.en: You paid last time? [[Fair enough]], I'll pay.
ex.tr: Geçen sefer sen mi ödedin? Tamam, ben öderim.

ex.en: [[Fair enough]], but I still don't like it.
ex.tr: Tamam, mantıklı, ama yine de hoşuma gitmiyor.
